descriptions.text: The Bard's Golden Throat – Enchanted Headset Microphone. Nuclear power. The airplane. Transistors. Antibiotics. Important inventions and discoveries of the 1900's that changed the world. But those were nothing, absolutely nothing, compared to the greatest invention of the century. It happened in September of 1997. That was the day it all changed. That was the day a company called Antares Audio Technologies released into the wild a piece of software that finally cured a horrific disability that'd been plaguing young men and women for a millennia. The disability? Tone deafness. The cure? It was called AutoTune. …

beats.headline: A real one this time
beats.text: Donut's platinum fan box opens and she bounces with excitement: her Princess Posse voted on it, and it is a real one, not the prop she used at the party, with a purple jewel on it. She will look just like Britney, the real one. It is the Bard's Golden Throat, carrying the Golden Throat enchantment, the dungeon's autotune, which Mordecai went looking for on the sixth floor and never found. It tunes songs within a step and a half of the note, assists bard songs and spells, amplifies speech and song two to five times, and adds five per cent Charisma. Equipped, it makes her sound like she is talking through a fan.

beats.headline: A secret weapon
beats.text: Donut discovers she can make her voice even louder, and Mongo screeches. Carl looks up at the ceiling and suggests they keep it as a secret weapon. She supposes he is right. The headset goes into her inventory, on her hotlist, to put on when she needs a little extra oomph, or when he is not paying attention to her properly.

beats.headline: Limbered
beats.text: Among the ghommids, with Carl's back patch fed again, Donut sings from his shoulder, her voice electronic with autotune: she will protect her pretties, with her voice of an angel and her expertly sung ditties. It works. The party is limbered, its dexterity up by half. Still amplified and autotuned, Donut tells Carl to be quiet, because she needs to sing another verse to stack it. The second verse loses its rhyme, the boost is cancelled because the bard cannot hold a tune, and she is muted from singing for five minutes. She pulls the headset away.

beats.headline: Orders from a distance
beats.text: At the door of the turkey barn Carl tells Donut to get Clockwork Triplicate ready and pull out her microphone, and the headset poofs onto her head. She cannot cast while her deck is summoned, and her bard songs will not work either, because they must be activated from her interface. But they have found that with the headset on she can still amplify her voice and give orders from a distance.

beats.headline: Full setting
beats.text: Amayon has Carl and Samantha in his hand, and Carl knows that any spell he casts will make the demon drop him or squeeze harder. Then Donut bellows at the demon at the top of her lungs, headset microphone at the full setting, autotune on. He orders her to turn off her spell or be obliterated. She will, she shouts back, if he lets her friends go.

beats.headline: Auto-Tune to the max
beats.text: Carl and Donut are to sing one of the guild-entrance songs, one listed with two singers, so that each of them has a performance bar. Carl takes the lead, because Donut has only a few lines and her chances are higher. She will use her headset with the Auto-Tune turned to the max, and Carl has to read a scroll, Gelded Choirboy, to hit the notes at all. Before they start, she raises the headset's volume and asks the crowd to encourage Carl: this is his first time singing ever, she tells them.

beats.headline: Take on me
beats.text: When the chorus comes, Donut echoes Carl's line, her Auto-Tuned voice high and, thankfully, in key, piercing the chaos of the brawl in the bar like a knife. At the same moment she shoots a low-powered magic missile that blows an axe out of the hand of a Draconian about to sink it into the back of Dong's head.

beats.headline: Borrowed, Auto-Tune off
beats.text: When Prepotente's song ends and it is Carl's turn, he taps the headset microphone he has borrowed from Donut, its Auto-Tune turned off for this. His voice reverberates over the stands as Hedy's truck passes, and he tells them what he told Donut about the difference between revenge and vengeance.
